subject: Urgent: chunked-transfer stalls causing elevated latency & errors
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@brightedge.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@brightedge.ai
Date: 2028-07-17T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Realtime stalls: chunked transfer stalls and 504s on our trial

Vanessa,

We started a larger pilot yesterday and are seeing significant problems with the streaming output: the WebSocket/Chunked responses hang intermittently and after ~25-40s a 504 or connection drop occurs. Impact: 20-30% request error rate, and median latency for token delivery has spiked from ~120ms to >900ms. This affects both our realtime assistant and the gallery live preview.

Attached is a small log sample and a HAR from one failed session (logs_20280717.zip).

This is hitting our users and we need an urgent path to stabilize — ideally something that can be applied in the next couple hours. If you need access to additional traces or want us to flip something on our side (e.g., disable streaming), say the word.

We also need executive visibility if this will take longer. Aaron

Aaron Lee
Head of Integrations, BrightEdge AI
aaron.lee@brightedge.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-17T09:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stalls: chunked transfer stalls and 504s on our trial

Hi Aaron — thanks for the heads up and the logs. This is currently high priority for us. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (SRE) to triage immediately; Aditya is on the account for commercial/credit coordination.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether you saw the failures across multiple regions or a single region?
- Can you reproduce with a single small request (we can provide a test token if helpful)?

Initial plan: Marissa/Karthik to surface any quick config mitigations we can flip (proxy/chunking, keepalive), then we will propose a short-term mitigation (minutes → hours) and a longer fix (code/kernel rollback or full patch). Ill update BrightEdge before we take any action.

We will stand up a 30-minute triage call in ~15 min — if that works for you I will send a calendar invite.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-17T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stalls: chunked transfer stalls and 504s on our trial

Thanks Vanessa — I pulled the account traces and reproduced the pattern in our staging ingest. High-level notes:
- Symptoms: long-tail pauses where the socket is open but no chunks arrive for 20–40s, then connection resets or client-side timeout.
- Correlation: these incidents cluster around times where the proxy coalesces small token frames into larger chunks (we see a batching/windowing heuristic firing).
- Hypothesis: proxy_max_chunk_delay is too large for this workload; small responses are being held to aggregate I/O, creating head-of-line stalls under bursty traffic.

Quick mitigation we can push immediately (config-only, no deploy): reduce proxy_max_chunk_delay from 1500ms to 200ms and enable aggressive keepalive pings for this specific pool. This is a rolling config change; I expect improvement within 5–10 minutes of the change. I attached a short diff with the config we used for a test cluster (patch_lower_chunk_delay.diff).

If that doesn't resolve it, fallback option is to expose a poll-based endpoint for this account (no streaming) until we complete a kernel replay/rollback. Polling preserves correctness but will increase per-token latency; we can cap concurrency to protect stability.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stalls: chunked transfer stalls and 504s on our trial

Adding technical color from infra — thanks Marissa. Observations:
- We rolled a kernel/runtime selection tweak last night (kernel v3.11 candidate) that altered stream flushing semantics and reduced the heartbeat/flush cadence on certain model shims. That could amplify proxy coalescing effects.
- Metrics: host-level TX buffers show bursts aligning with elevated token latency; connection-level keepalive timeouts tick before the next chunk is produced.

Mitigation options and ETA:
- Immediate (~~15–30m): apply Marissas config changes (lower chunk delay + enable keepalives) to the affected pool. No service restart; rolling config push.
- Short window (~2–4 hours): enable per-account streaming throttle and temporarily disable aggressive coalescing in the proxy for BrightEdge AI. Minor risk to throughput but reduces stalls.
- Rollback path (next-day scheduled change): revert the kernel change (requires coordination and a brief window) — this will address the root cause if the kernel change is the primary vector.

I've created a Jira ticket: JIRA-RED-2345 and linked traces. I'll push the config change now to a canary behind a flag; if green, we can widen within 30–45 minutes.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-17T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Update: immediate mitigation in progress for BrightEdge AI — timeline & credits

Aaron — quick update for BrightEdge stakeholders: our SRE team has pushed a canary config (proxy_max_chunk_delay -> 200ms + keepalives enabled) to one node in your serving pool. We are monitoring the canary now. Expected behavior: token delivery tail will tighten and the 504s should drop substantially within ~15m if this is the dominant factor.

If the canary looks good, plan is to widen to the rest of the pool over the next 30–45 minutes. If you prefer we can also flip a temporary non-streaming (poll) fallback for your workspace — that is slightly higher latency but removes the streaming tail entirely while we validate.

We will be offering a one-month credit on usage for any production-impacting errors during the incident window; Aditya will coordinate the paperwork if we need to escalate commercially.

Apologies for the disruption — we are treating this as an exec-level priority until fully resolved. I will follow up once the canary is green/widened or if we detect a regression.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@brightedge.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-18T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Update: immediate mitigation in progress for BrightEdge AI — timeline & credits

Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turn. Canary looked good for our test traffic. Please go ahead and widen. We will accept the temporary poll fallback if you detect instability during the rollout.

Please send the incident summary and the postmortem link when ready; we will need that for our internal stakeholder update.

Aaron
Aaron Lee
Head of Integrations, BrightEdge AI
